question: Should requester-scoped MCP become a permanent public plugin SDK contract with duplicate registrations rejected and a documented five-minute revocation-revalidation SLA?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but automation cannot choose permanent resolver ownership or the acceptable authorization-revocation window for external plugins.

options.title: Fail duplicates and approve SLA
options.body: Reject duplicate server-name registrations, document the five-minute maximum core revalidation window, and approve the public requester-scoped API.

options.title: Approve current semantics
options.body: Keep warning-plus-replacement registration and the five-minute window as intentional, documented plugin contracts.

options.title: Defer the public API
options.body: Pause the PR until resolver ownership and revocation requirements are redesigned behind a narrower experimental or internal seam.

recommendation.title: Fail duplicates and approve SLA
recommendation.body: Reject duplicate server-name registrations, document the five-minute maximum core revalidation window, and approve the public requester-scoped API.
